recipes.name: Vasilopita - Greek New Years Cake
ingredients_raw: 1 cup warm milk (110 degrees F/45 degrees C)

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Generously grease a 10-inch round cake pan.

Beat sugar and butter together in a medium bowl until lighter in color; stir in flour and mix until the mixture is mealy. Add eggs one at a time, mixing well after each addition. Combine baking powder and milk; add to egg mixture, mix well. Combine lemon juice and baking soda; stir into the batter. Pour into the prepared cake pan.

Bake in the preheated oven for 20 minutes. Remove and sprinkle the nuts and sugar over the cake, then return it to the oven until cake springs back to the touch, about 20 to 30 additional minutes. Gently cut a small hole in the cake and place a quarter in the hole. Try to cover the hole with sugar. Cool cake on a rack for 10 minutes before inverting onto a plate.

raw_recipe.headline: Vasilopita - Greek New Years Cake
raw_recipe.description: Vasilopita is a traditional Greek New Year's Day cake served for breakfast. Whoever receives the coin hidden inside gets good luck for the whole year!

review.reviewBody: Fantastic recipe!I am greek,living in Athens,was looking for a new vassilopita recipe and tried this one...my husband said it is the best he ever had,my children loved it,it was consumed on the spot,even after a rich new year's dinner! I topped it with our favorite creem cheese frosting,and wrote on top of it 2007 as is the tradition,using mini m+m's.Should have taken a picture!

Made this potential family annual tradition in a springform pan which eliminated the tricky inversion process.
Also substituted a whole almond for the lucky quarter (which would have required pre-santitizing).

I love this cake and it’s fun to make! I’ve made it three times and it turned out great every time. I did add 1/2 teaspoon almond extract even though I like it without also, used a springform pan as it rises that high, I put it on a cookie sheet as it did leak just a tad, baked it 65minutes.

I used Almond Extract instead of Lemon. I cut back on the sugar by about a 1/4 Cup. I also added about a Cup of sliced almonds to the batter right before putting it in the pan to bake. Instead of granulated sugar, I used powdered sugar right before serving. Baked in a spring form pan placed on parchment paper on a cookie sheet for about an hour. I will definitely make this again.

Made this cake for New Year's gifts for neighbors and it was fantastic! I used two 6" round pans and it looked just beautiful. Bake time was still about the same, although I did the sugar/almonds at about 18 minutes instead of 20 so they would stick better. Thought sliced almonds looked prettier than slivered as the recipe listed. Enjoy!

I had to host a New Years party at my sisters house. I had to come up with idea for the icing . Used carnal Apple topping on the cake. They boys were allergic to nuts. So I thought outside the bag. I took some Oreo cookies and grounded them up in the food blender. When they were done. I used them as a topping for this cake. They wanted a toy baby didn’t have one. So I used a Macintosh cherry and baked i it into the cake. It was extremely yummy and a big hit at the party. Whoever found the cherry won the cool prize.

It was fantastic, although I did add almond extract to the batter for a more almond-y flavor. It was a big hit at the New Years party! I did substitute a whole almond for the coin due to excessive drinking on New Years :) I originally put it in a springform pan but it started to leak in my oven! In a pinch I put it in a bundt pan, which turned out just fine. Excellent cake, not too sweet, needs no icing but would be good with an almond flavored glaze. Happy baking, and eating! :)

This recipe turned out great. A couple things I did different is I actually sifted the flower because I had read several recipes that talked about sifting it which helped it be fluffier. I also don't think you need to have those two tablespoons of sugar to spread on the top. I did add it this time but in future I would leave that last two tablespoons off cuz it didn't add anything. I actually sprinkled some powdered sugar on top after it was baked and cooled. I cut out some parchment paper with the letters of the year and then I did the powdered sugar around it. And the only thing I added was a half teaspoon of vanilla. But my mother loved it and so did i. It was moist and Light and delicious. It is definitely a keeper. Jan 2025

I made this in a large round stoneware baker which was a perfect size, but I needed to give it some extra baking time, which made it a tad dry. It makes quite a large cake, great for breakfast with jam and coffee. I agree with another reviewer that it was moister the second and third days. I would make it ahead.

Great recipe, I modified it a bit by adding a teaspoon of almond extract to the batter,adding half a cup of evaporated milk and half a cup of heavy whipping cream instead of the cup of milk, and I made icing instead of using powdered sugar. I made the icing my using a can of sweetened milk, a quarter cup of heavy whipping cream, and a half cup of evaporated milk, then I added a teaspoon of almond extract. I boiled and stirred the ingredients until it became thick enough to glaze the cake, and I applied it as I would have applied the sugar then topped the cake with almonds.

This was my first vasilopita, so I wasn't sure what to expect. It was delicious, essentially a pound cake. I saw that many reviewers noted it took much longer to bake than the recipe called for, so I decided to be clever and make it in a two-part tube pan like you make angel food cake in. I figured that the hole in the center would help it bake through in the time given. Well, sort of. instead, as many reviewers stated about the springform pan called for, the batter leaked out. (Fortunately, in case of that, I had placed the pan on a parchment-lined baking sheet, so no mess in my oven). 
But what DID happen was that the leaking batter went up the center of the tube, making its own mini-cake. Perhaps because of the leaking, the cake was not as tall as I hoped. At least we got the mini-cake to taste-test before taking the full-cake to a New Year's brunch! The cake got good reviews, and I will make it again. 
Aside from the pan, the only thing I did different was to grate a little orange zest into the batter. Next time I think I will use a Bundt pan, and will dust with powdered sugar rather than granulated.

The cake was very easy to make!! I did boil a 'newer' quarter and placed it into the cake when it was hot out of the oven and covered the area with sugar. I HOPE I find it!! :) The flavor is very good, simple, and I liked it but did not love it. Maybe be good pouring a 'sugar syrup' over it after it has baked? I don't like changing recipes though so won't make it again. But I did enjoy it. Thank you for the recipe!! :)

This came out a bit dense. It raised an eyebrow to mix the baking soda and lemon juice before adding to the batter. It foamed up just like your chemistry teacher said it would, and I'm guessing that neutralized it as a raising agent.
I added the zest of 2 lemons and 1 tsp of lemon extract. It was a hit at my New Year brunch!
It was really good! I made it in a Bundt pan. I did need to bake it longer, about 15 minutes. But I didn’t think it was dry, and it was plenty sweet.

Delicious! A new tradition is born for my family! (I hid a whole almond instead of a coin)
Thank you for this lovely recipe.

I made this to bring in the new year! I did make a substitute as I didn’t have lemon juice. I added 1 teaspoon of almond extract and topped with powdered sugar. Does need to be naked longer as suggested by others. Delicious!
